text:
sqmeow.nvim

 

A lightweight database client that lives inside Neovim. Browse databases, run queries, edit data, and explore results without leaving your editor.

If you spend most of your time in the terminal and don't want to switch to a GUI just to inspect a few rows, sqmeow.nvim is for you.

 Preview

 
 Screenshots 

 Overview

 

 Editing results

 

 Table structure

 

 

 Features

- Multiple databases: Work with SQL, NoSQL, and analytical databases in one place.
- Interactive results: Browse, filter, sort, and edit data directly in Neovim.
- Query history: Revisit previous results without running queries again.
- Local result processing: Filter and sort retained rows using Polars.
- Project-local connections: Keep connections and scratchpads alongside your project.
- Completion: Database-aware suggestions with blink.cmp or nvim-cmp.
- Rust engine: Database operations run in a separate Rust process.

 Supported databases

- Relational and analytical: PostgreSQL, CockroachDB, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, DuckDB, ClickHouse, Oracle Database, Microsoft SQL Server.
- Key-value and document: Redis, Valkey, Dragonfly, MongoDB, SurrealDB.
- Wide-column: ScyllaDB, Cassandra.

 Installation

Requires Neovim 0.10+ and nui.nvim. nvim-treesitter is optional and enables query-aware autocomplete.

Calling setup() is optional unless you want to customize the defaults.

 
 lazy.nvim 

 

 

 
 vim.pack (Neovim 0.12+) 

 

 

The install hook downloads the matching engine release. Prebuilt binaries are available for Linux (x86 64/ARM64), macOS (Apple Silicon), and Windows (x86 64).

To track master with lazy.nvim or vim.pack, remove the release version setting and use install("cargo") .

After installation, run :checkhealth sqmeow to verify your setup. Use :Sqmeow restart after rebuilding the engine.

 Getting started

1. Run :Sqmeow to open the drawer and results window.
2. Press A in the drawer to add a database connection.
3. Press to connect, then u to select it for queries.
4. Press a to create a scratchpad, write a query, and press to execute it.

Use visual to execute selected text, or E to execute the entire buffer.

 Help

The full manual ships as Vim help. Start with :h sqmeow for the table of contents. :h sqmeow-keymaps lists every mapping and shows how to override it, and :h sqmeow-commands covers the commands.

Press ? in the drawer or result window to see the mappings for that window.

 Working with results

 Editing

Edit cells directly in the result grid, review your changes, and apply them when ready.

Editing requires table-backed columns and a complete primary or unique key. Availability varies by database adapter. For server-enforced read-only access, use a read-only database account.

 Filtering and sorting

sqmeow.nvim uses Polars SQL to filter and sort retained results locally, including results from query history.

Explore data without rerunning the original query or losing staged edits. Rerun the query when you need fresh data.

 Query languages

Each database uses its own query language:

- SQL databases use their respective SQL dialects.
- Redis accepts one command per line.
- MongoDB accepts Extended JSON commands.
- ScyllaDB and Cassandra use CQL.
- SurrealDB uses SurrealQL.

For more details, see :h sqmeow-queries .

 Connections

Add and save connections through the drawer, or define project-specific connections in .sqmeow/connections.toml :

 

The nearest project configuration overrides saved connections with the same name. The plugin resolves relative database paths from the project root.

 Credentials

A connection can also use a database URL:

 

Set DATABASE URL in your environment or in a .env file next to .sqmeow/ . Environment variables take precedence over values in .env .

Keep .env out of version control, and reconnect after changing credentials.

 SSH tunnels

To connect through SSH, set ssh = "user@bastion" or use a Host alias from /.ssh/config . The plugin resolves the database host from the SSH host.

See :h sqmeow-project and :h sqmeow-credentials for all connection options.

 Scratchpads

Store project queries in .sqmeow/scratchpads/ using .sql , .redis , .json , or .surql files.

Create, rename, and delete them from the drawer. :h sqmeow-keymaps lists the scratchpad mappings.

Queries run against the currently selected connection.

 Completion

Use blink.cmp or nvim-cmp for database-aware completion.

For query-aware suggestions, install the SQL Tree-sitter parser with :TSInstall sql via nvim-treesitter.

 
 blink.cmp 

 

 

 
 nvim-cmp 

 

 

See :h sqmeow-completion for more details.

 Statusline

sqmeow.nvim exposes the current buffer's state as a plain table, so you can render connection and query status in any statusline: lualine.nvim, heirline, mini.statusline , or a custom 'statusline' .

 require("sqmeow.api.view").status() returns nil outside database buffers, and require("sqmeow.api.view").column() returns the active result column and SQL type, or "" .

If your statusline already shows this, you can disable winbars completely ( ui = { winbar = false } ) or control them per window ( ui = { winbar = { editor = false, result = true, show connection = false } } ).

 
 lualine.nvim 

 

 

 

 
 What status() returns 

 

 status() returns nil outside database buffers. staged changes counts edits across all open results, column is set only in the result grid, and state /row counts describe the call whose connection matches the buffer.

 

See :h sqmeow.api.view.status() and :h sqmeow.api.view.column() for more details.

 Configuration

Customize behavior with setup() .

Common options with their defaults:

 

 max rows limits the number of retained rows, while page size controls how many rows appear per page.

Set max rows = 0 for unlimited rows or timeout ms = 0 to disable query deadlines.

See :h sqmeow-config for all configuration options and :h sqmeow-keymaps for custom keymaps.

install.title: Installation
install.html:
Requires Neovim 0.10+ and nui.nvim. nvim-treesitter is optional and enables query-aware autocomplete.

Calling setup() is optional unless you want to customize the defaults.

lazy.nvim
{
  "2giosangmitom/sqmeow.nvim",
  version = "*",
  dependencies = { "MunifTanjim/nui.nvim" },
  build = function()
    require("sqmeow").install()
  end,
  opts = {},
  cmd = "Sqmeow",
}
vim.pack (Neovim 0.12+)
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("PackChanged", {
  callback = function(event)
    local data = event.data
    if data.spec.name ~= "sqmeow.nvim" or (data.kind ~= "install" and data.kind ~= "update") then
      return
    end

    vim.schedule(function()
      require("sqmeow").install()
    end)
  end,
})

vim.pack.add({
  "https://github.com/MunifTanjim/nui.nvim",
  {
    src = "https://github.com/2giosangmitom/sqmeow.nvim",
    version = vim.version.range(">=0.0.0"),
  },
})

The install hook downloads the matching engine release. Prebuilt binaries are available for Linux (x86_64/ARM64), macOS (Apple Silicon), and Windows (x86_64).

To track master with lazy.nvim or vim.pack, remove the release version setting and use install("cargo").

After installation, run :checkhealth sqmeow to verify your setup. Use :Sqmeow restart after rebuilding the engine.
